preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner or an authorized address (via the authorized modifier)
Attacker must hold some CRACE tokens to trigger fee collection

violation_target.exploit_hint: As an authorized address, call setFees() with extremely high fee percentages (e.g., 9900 for each fee component) and a low feeDenominator (e.g., 10000). Then execute a token transfer to trigger fee collection. The high fees will cause most of the transferred tokens to be collected as fees, which are then converted to BNB and sent to marketingFeeReceiver (which can be set to attacker's address via setFeeReceivers()). Alternatively, use rescueBNB() as owner to drain contract BNB balance.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract has multiple owner/authorized functions that can be abused. The setFees() function allows setting extremely high fee percentages, and setFeeReceivers() allows setting the marketing fee receiver to the attacker's address. When a token transfer occurs, high fees are collected, converted to BNB, and sent to the marketing fee receiver (attacker).
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate an authorized address, set fees to near 100%, set marketing fee receiver to attacker, acquire some CRACE tokens, and trigger a transfer to collect massive fees that get converted to BNB and sent to attacker.
attempts.step_by_step_plan:
1. Impersonate owner (who is authorized by default)
2. Set fees to 9900 each with denominator 10000 (99% total fee)
3. Set marketing fee receiver to attacker address
4. Get some CRACE tokens via deal()
5. Transfer tokens to trigger fee collection
6. The contract will accumulate fees and eventually swap them to BNB
7. Marketing portion of BNB will be sent to attacker
